prompt:
Write 9 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a rear-end collision claim, in time order. Injury: wrist fracture. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1354; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment ran somewhat longer than usual for this injury.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- A neighbor thinks the car was damaged some weeks before the claimed date.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Insured reported a rear-end collision at a low-speed intersection. The claimant's attorney has notified us of representation and asked that all contact go through their office.

Entry 2: Photos from the scene show damage to the rear bumper and trunk area that lines up with the impact described. The police report confirms the claimant was in the vehicle at the time of the collision.

Entry 3: Repair estimate has been received and the damage pattern is consistent with the reported impact. No prior damage to the vehicle is known from our records or the prior-claims search.

Entry 4: Claimant reports a wrist injury and was diagnosed with a fracture. The force of the crash appears consistent with this type of injury, and no earlier injury to the same area is on file.

Entry 5: Treatment has continued for somewhat longer than is typical for this injury. Medical records are being requested to review the treatment timeline and any follow-up visits.

Entry 6: A neighbor contacted us saying they believe the car already had damage several weeks before the reported date of loss. This is an unverified recollection and has not been confirmed by any other source.

Entry 7: The claimant has given the same account of the collision in each conversation so far, including the first call, the recorded statement, and the follow-up with counsel present. No independent witnesses have come forward, so the account rests on the parties and the physical evidence.

Entry 8: The driver is listed on the policy, and coverage for the date of loss has been confirmed. Liability questions remain open pending the review of the photos and the police report.

Entry 9: File is under review. Next steps include obtaining the complete medical records, following up on the neighbor's comments, and scheduling a final evaluation of the injury claim with the claimant's attorney.
